priority_actions.title: Launch 'Gold Rush Picnic Kits' targeting Nevada Theatre (62m) and Hot Summer Nights festival crowds
priority_actions.what: Create three ready-to-go picnic bundles priced at $18, $28, and $42. Each includes items already in stock: wine or beer from the full liquor cabinet, Amy's pizza or snack items, and one specialty item. Label them 'The Prospector,' 'The Bonanza,' and 'The Motherlode.' Place them behind the counter. Post a sign at the entrance: 'Heading to Nevada Theatre or Hot Summer Nights? Grab a picnic kit.' Hot Summer Nights runs the last three Wednesdays of July. Nevada Theatre is 62 meters from your front door. Print 50 small cards to leave at the National Hotel (161m) and Friar Tuck's (88m) listing the bundle options.
priority_actions.why: Nevada City's Hot Summer Nights festival draws crowds to Broad St on Wednesday evenings in July. Nevada Theatre at 62m is California's oldest operating theater and hosts shows year-round. Tourists already walk past Bonanza Market's door. The bundle creates a single high-margin transaction ($18-$42) vs. a $4 impulse buy. Three price points anchor perception — the $28 'Bonanza' becomes the default choice.
priority_actions.money_estimate: $8,000-$18,000/year. Math: 15 kits/week at avg $28 = $420/week × 20 peak weeks = $8,400 base; event weeks at 30 kits = $16,800 ceiling.
priority_actions.cost: $200 one-time for signage and printed cards

priority_actions.title: Partner with National Hotel (161m) and Friar Tuck's (88m) for a 'Late Night Essentials' referral program
priority_actions.what: Walk into the National Hotel and Friar Tuck's Restaurant this week and propose a mutual referral arrangement. Bonanza Market is the only full-service general store in Nevada City per its own Google reviews. Hotel guests who need last-minute items (medicine, wine, snacks) after restaurant kitchens close need a nearby option. Ask the National Hotel front desk to keep 10 Bonanza Market cards at check-in: 'Need wine, beer, or basics? Bonanza Market is 2 minutes away.' In return, post a framed 'Where to Eat Tonight' card near Bonanza Market's register pointing to Friar Tuck's and Lika's Quarter Cafe (49m) — builds goodwill and repeat foot traffic.
priority_actions.why: The National Hotel is described by the Nevada City Chamber as 'the state's oldest, continuously operated hotel' and sits 161m from Bonanza Market. Friar Tuck's is 88m away. Hotel guests without a car and diners finishing late are captured customer segments that no competitor can serve — Winnie Superette (0.04mi) focuses on curated housewares and specialty snacks, not full-service general merchandise. Bonanza Market's extended product range (meds, wine, spirits, food) is the differentiator.
priority_actions.money_estimate: $5,000-$12,000/year. Math: 10 additional tourist transactions/week at avg $22 = $220/week × 50 weeks = $11,000.

priority_actions.money_estimate: $3,000-$6,000/year retained. Math: 5 lost regulars/year at $60/month avg spend = $3,600 in retained revenue; clearance sales recover ~$800-$1,200 in margin.

enriched_recommendations.what: Launch a paper punch card loyalty program this week. Print 200 cards — buy 9 items, get the 10th free (up to $12 value). Hand one to every customer at checkout. enriched_recommendations.why_it_works: When a customer holds a physical punch card with their name on it, they experience a sense of ownership over an in-progress reward that makes leaving feel like a loss rather than a neutral choice. This is the endowment effect combined with commitment-and-consistency: once a person has started a punch card, they are psychologically committed to completing it. For a general store in a small historic-district town where residents make 3-5 weekly trips, the punch card converts each individual transaction into a link in a behavioral chain that keeps customers walking past Winnie Superette and SPD Markets to complete their card at Bonanza.

enriched.local_context: Bonanza Market occupies a prime position on Broad St in Nevada City's national historic landmark downtown district, 62 meters from California's oldest operating theater and steps from the National Hotel, one of the oldest continuously operated hotels west of the Rockies. Nevada City draws a steady flow of Gold Country tourists from Sacramento and the Bay Area, with a peak season running July through September, anchored by the Hot Summer Nights festival (last three Wednesdays in July), the Nevada City Film Festival in fall, and the Victorian Christmas street fair in December. key_risks.early_warning_sign: Check Google Maps 'grocery' search results weekly on a mobile phone in Nevada City. If Bonanza appears below Winnie Superette or SPD Markets in the local pack, the rating gap is actively costing walk-in traffic.
key_risks.mitigation: Launch an in-store review ask program within 7 days: print a small card at checkout with a QR code linking directly to the Google review page. Target 10 new reviews in 30 days to push toward 4.3+ stars and 137+ total reviews.
key_risks.cost_if_ignored: Estimated $800–$1,500/month in lost new-customer revenue as higher-rated competitors capture first-visit grocery spend from the 3,172-person ZIP and tourist foot traffic to Nevada Theatre and National Hotel.

key_risks.risk_title: No website means zero search capture from Nevada Theatre and National Hotel foot traffic
key_risks.description: Bonanza Market has no website listed on Google. Nearby venues — Nevada Theatre, National Hotel, Friar Tuck's, Stonehouse Restaurant — generate foot traffic from out-of-town visitors who search 'specialty food near Nevada Theatre' or 'grocery Nevada City' before arriving. Without a website, Bonanza cannot rank in organic search, cannot show hours/offerings, and cannot be linked from hotel concierge recommendation pages. Winnie Superette (0.04mi, 4.9 stars) captures this zero-click intent by default.
key_risks.early_warning_sign: Google your business name weekly. If the Knowledge Panel shows 'No website' and Winnie Superette or SPD Markets appear above Bonanza in 'grocery Nevada City' searches, tourist capture is being lost every week.
key_risks.mitigation: Create a free Google Business Profile website or a one-page site on Squarespace/Wix within 30 days. Include hours, address, a photo of the store, and 3–5 specialty product callouts. Submit the URL to Google Business Profile immediately.
key_risks.cost_if_ignored: $500–$2,000/month in missed tourist and visitor grocery spend, plus zero chance of National Hotel or venue concierge referrals that require a linkable web presence.

key_risks.risk_title: Summer peak season July–September understaffed or under-inventoried without event demand triggers
key_risks.description: Peak season runs July–September with August the single highest-traffic month. With no upcoming events on the calendar within 10 miles over the next 90 days, Bonanza has no external demand signals to plan inventory and staffing around — meaning stock-outs or understaffing during the highest-revenue months go undetected until they happen. A single weekend of empty shelves on specialty items or long checkout lines during August peak could push 4.1 stars to 3.9, crossing the psychological threshold that suppresses Google rankings.
key_risks.early_warning_sign: Track weekly transaction count and average basket size starting June 1. If July week-1 transactions are up more than 15% over June average, accelerate reorder cycles immediately for top 10 SKUs.
key_risks.mitigation: By June 30, build a simple peak-season inventory buffer: identify the top 10 specialty SKUs by margin, increase order quantities by 20% for July and August, and cross-train one additional staff member on checkout and stocking.
key_risks.cost_if_ignored: $1,000–$3,000 in lost peak-season sales from stock-outs, plus 3–6 negative reviews during the highest-visibility tourist months that take months to offset.

key_risks.risk_title: Winnie Superette at 0.04mi pulling impulse and convenience purchases daily
key_risks.description: Winnie Superette operates 0.04 miles from Bonanza — essentially the same block on Broad St — with a 4.9-star rating on 43 reviews. For any customer choosing between the two for a quick convenience purchase, Winnie's higher rating is visible on Google Maps before they walk through either door. Bonanza's 4.1 rating is a 0.8-star gap that represents a meaningful perceived quality difference to first-time shoppers. Without differentiation on signage, social proof, or specialty offerings, Bonanza loses the daily impulse customer by default.
key_risks.early_warning_sign: Stand outside the store on a Saturday morning for 20 minutes and count foot traffic entering Winnie Superette versus Bonanza. If the ratio exceeds 2:1 in Winnie's favor, the street-level conversion gap is real and worsening.
key_risks.mitigation: Within 30 days, add exterior signage or a sidewalk A-frame highlighting 2–3 specialty products not available at Winnie Superette (e.g., local produce, specific deli items, or unique brands). Differentiate on product, not price.
key_risks.cost_if_ignored: $600–$1,200/month in lost impulse convenience revenue diverted to Winnie Superette on walk-by traffic alone.

key_risks.risk_title: Nevada City Farmers Market drawing loyal local grocery spend every market day
key_risks.description: Nevada City Farmers Market operates 0.15mi from Bonanza with 4.7 stars and 88 reviews — more reviews than Bonanza and a higher rating. In a small-population ZIP of 3,172 residents with median income of $75,792, a health- and quality-conscious customer base allocates discretionary food spending to the Farmers Market on market days. This pulls the exact high-value local shopper Bonanza needs for repeat business. Without a clear reason to visit Bonanza on market days (complementary products, prepared foods, or market-day specials), Bonanza loses those customers entirely.
key_risks.early_warning_sign: Check foot traffic on Farmers Market days versus non-market days by counting transactions. If market-day transactions are more than 20% lower than average non-market weekday, the market is actively pulling customers away.
key_risks.mitigation: Within 30 days, create a 'Market Day Complement' promotion — items the Farmers Market doesn't sell (cooking staples, packaged goods, beverages) at a visible in-store display near the entrance, with a small A-frame outside on market days.
key_risks.cost_if_ignored: $400–$900/month in regular-customer grocery spend lost to Farmers Market on 2–4 market days per month.

key_risks.risk_title: 4.1-star rating vulnerable to 1–2 negative reviews dropping below 4.0
key_risks.description: At 127 reviews and 4.1 stars, Bonanza sits close to the 4.0 threshold. A single 1-star review drops the average to approximately 4.08 stars; two in quick succession could push below 4.0. Google's local pack algorithm deprioritizes sub-4.0 results in competitive searches. Given that Garnish Nevada City (5.0), Levity Health Market (5.0), and Winnie Superette (4.9) all operate nearby, a sub-4.0 rating would make Bonanza effectively invisible to new customers searching on Google Maps.
key_risks.early_warning_sign: Check Google reviews every Monday morning. Any new 1- or 2-star review should trigger an owner response within 48 hours and an immediate internal review of the complaint to prevent recurrence.
key_risks.mitigation: Within 14 days, set up a free Google Alerts notification or bookmark the Google Business Profile review tab. Respond to all existing unanswered negative reviews this week with a professional, specific reply to show prospective customers the issue was addressed.
key_risks.cost_if_ignored: A drop below 4.0 stars could reduce new-customer walk-ins by an estimated 15–25%, representing $700–$1,800/month in lost revenue in a low-population market with limited replacement customer volume.

execution_templates.template_title: In-store review ask card script for checkout staff
execution_templates.when_to_use: Use at the end of every transaction, after handing the customer their bag. Works best when the customer says something positive about a product or the store.
execution_templates.body: "Thanks so much! Quick favor — we're trying to grow our Google reviews. Would you mind leaving us one? I can text you the link right now. Takes about 30 seconds."
execution_templates.success_metric: Target 10 new Google reviews in 30 days. If fewer than 3 reviews after week 1, add a QR code card at the register and hand it to every customer.

execution_templates.template_title: Text message to send review link to willing customers
execution_templates.when_to_use: Send immediately after a customer agrees at checkout to leave a Google review. Staff sends from store phone or owner's phone.
execution_templates.body: Hi! Here's our Google review link for Bonanza Market — takes 30 sec: [INSERT GOOGLE REVIEW DIRECT LINK] Thanks so much! — [your name], Bonanza Market
execution_templates.success_metric: Target 1 completed review per 3 texts sent. If completion rate drops below 1 in 5, shorten the message and confirm the link works on both iPhone and Android.

execution_templates.template_title: Loyalty punch card enrollment script for returning customers
execution_templates.when_to_use: Use with any customer you recognize as a repeat visitor, or any customer spending over $20. Deliver at the end of the transaction.
execution_templates.body: "We just started a loyalty card — buy [number, e.g. 8] times and your [specific reward, e.g. next deli order] is on us. Want me to start you one today? Just takes your name."
execution_templates.success_metric: Enroll 20 repeat customers in the first 30 days. If fewer than 5 enrolled in week 1, move the pitch to the start of the transaction when energy is higher.

execution_templates.template_title: Email to nearby venues (National Hotel, Nevada Theatre) proposing a local partner discount
execution_templates.when_to_use: Send to the manager or owner of National Hotel and Nevada Theatre within the next 7 days. Find contact info on their websites or visit in person.
execution_templates.subject: Local deal for your guests — Bonanza Market, right on Broad St
execution_templates.body:
Hi [contact name],

I'm [your name], owner of Bonanza Market at 321 Broad St — we're about a [2-minute walk / X-minute walk] from [National Hotel / Nevada Theatre].

I'd love to offer your guests a small perk: a [10%] discount card they can use at our store during their stay or visit. We carry specialty and local products that visitors tend to love, and it gives them something easy to do nearby.

No cost to you — I'll supply the cards. Could we set up a quick 10-minute chat this week?

Thanks,
[Your name]
[Your phone number]
Bonanza Market, 321 Broad St, Nevada City
execution_templates.success_metric: Target 1 confirmed partner out of every 4 emails sent. If no reply within 5 days, follow up with a 2-sentence in-person drop-in.

execution_templates.template_title: Text message to lapsed customers to bring them back
execution_templates.when_to_use: Send to any customer you have a phone number for who hasn't visited in 60+ days. Send on a Thursday or Friday before the weekend.
execution_templates.body: Hey [first name]! Haven't seen you in a while at Bonanza Market. Come in this week & show this text for [10%] off your order. — [your name], 321 Broad St
execution_templates.success_metric: Target 2 redemptions per 10 texts sent. If under 1 in 10 after the first send, change the offer to a free item (e.g., 'free coffee with any purchase') and resend to non-openers.
